highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 (unreleased) adds Graphite GPU backends, async pixel reads, and performance improvements.
highlights_body: This unreleased snapshot brings Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, a new async RequestReadPixels API, several managed-code performance wins, FreeType font support on Nano Server, and a new SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET package. Container-based test platforms (Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server) were added to the CI matrix.

bullets.detail: Multiple rounds of upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes have been synced into the engine.
New bindings expose the Graphite (next-gen) GPU backend for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, letting apps adopt Skia's modern rendering pipeline.
SKImage and SKSurface gain a backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels API, allowing GPU pixel data to be read back without stalling the GPU pipeline.
A new package integrates SkiaSharp with the Silk.NET Vulkan bindings, and Vulkan tests now run on Android and Linux CI legs.
All .sln solution files have been converted to the new .slnx format for better tooling compatibility.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support on Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server containers now get font rendering via FreeType, fixing a long-standing gap where text could not be rendered in that environment.

bullets.lead: Memory leak in SKImage.Create raster failure path fixed
bullets.detail: A CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak that occurred when the raster image creation failed has been corrected.

bullets.lead: Container test legs added: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: The CI matrix now includes containerized test runs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server, improving coverage for server and container deployment scenarios.

bullets.lead: Windows MSVC environment initialized once per native build
bullets.detail: The MSVC environment is now set up once per native build instead of per-step, reducing build times on Windows.
The default Windows SDK version pin has been lifted, allowing builds to use the SDK available in the environment.

bullets.lead: Performance: SKData.SaveTo avoids double buffer copy
bullets.detail: SaveTo now writes directly to the destination, eliminating an intermediate allocation and copy.

bullets.lead: Performance: allocation-free path in GetEncodedText and SKRuntimeEffectUniforms
bullets.detail: GetEncodedText no longer allocates an intermediate string in the null-terminated path; the SKRuntimeEffectUniforms lookup map is pre-sized to the known count.
